**Defending the original answer**

The conditional premise *“If you imagine and dream about something long and hard enough…”* describes only a mental activity. No additional premise states that any action will be taken, nor that the imagined thing has any causal power over reality.  

From a purely logical standpoint, the only conclusion that is **guaranteed** by the premise is that **nothing necessarily follows**; the imagined desire may remain purely internal.  

All other options (A, B, D, E) assert a specific external outcome (“you will get it”, “you will achieve it”, “it will happen”, “it will become real”). None of these outcomes is logically entailed by the premise, because imagination alone does not cause those results.  

Therefore the correct completion of the sentence is the option that states no guaranteed effect.

**Final answer:** C
